rubric.item: healthy ranges poker soundness and originality (sample-checked all 15)
locked TASK-10.1 edits only pass hand records (D-3)

findings.issue: The AC#2 check rounds the float percentage with Math.round(value*10) instead of the app's statTenths integer rule (A-1), and logs with console.log on every run.
findings.evidence: const tenths = Math.round((value as number) * 10); console.log(`TAG 6-max ${stat}: ...`). The measured margins are wide (≈22.2 in 20–28, etc.), so results do not change today, but the test does not use the same rounding the report shows.
findings.fix: Compute tenths with statTenths(part, whole) from the summed counts (same fractions as styleSection) and drop the console.log, or keep the log only on failure via the expect message. Locked test: change only if the orchestrator unlocks it.

findings.issue: A-7 covers both missing and invalid hand records; the test covers only an invalid one. The `get.result === undefined` branch in src/storage/hand-store.ts:99 is not exercised.
findings.evidence: corrupt() replaces hand 2 with {bad: true}; no case deletes a record.
findings.fix: Add a second damaged store where hand 2 is deleted (objectStore(HANDS_STORE).delete([SESSION, 2])) and assert style.handsDealt = 2 and the session ends.

findings.issue: APPROXIMATE_PLAYERS [3,4,5,7,8] and SIZE_NAMES restate the exact-size set and size names that also live in src/ui/config/GameConfigScreen.tsx (playersNote [2,6,9,10], TABLE_SIZE_NAMES). The headless module cannot import from ui, so this is the right direction, but there are now two copies that must stay in sync.
findings.fix: Optional later: have GameConfigScreen import the exact/approximate rule from a headless module (e.g. export isApproximateSize from src/advice/preflop.ts) so both use one source.

summary: All 15 SPEC items are implemented as specified and their tests would fail if the behaviour broke. Rounding (A-1): statTenths = floor((2000p+w)/(2w)) is exact half-up integer arithmetic, and rangeLabel compares the same tenths with low*10/high*10, both inclusive, so the shown value and its label always agree (28.0/20.0 in range, 28.1 too high, 19.9 too low, tested). endSession: the transaction now spans sessions, reports and hands; every hand get and the put/add run in request callbacks of the same strict transaction. A missing or unparseable record becomes null and is filtered out, so the session still ends (tested with a corrupt hand 2: handsDealt 2, endedAt stored, report readable). parseHandRecord guarantees the user seat is dealt in, so handsDealt >= 1 and the written style always passes parseStyle. endPausedSessions goes through the same ended(). Locked TASK-10.1 edits (tests/storage/session-end.acceptance.test.ts, e2e/session-report.spec.ts) only add the stored hand records as sessionReport's third argument, plus a type import. I ran e2e report-style, session-report and leave-mid-hand in Chromium and WebKit: 20/20 passed. The gate does not run e2e. Healthy ranges: these are plausible for fixed-limit play. 6-max VPIP 20-28 / PFR 14-22 and full ring 13-20 / 9-16 match a solid LHE TAG. Heads-up 65-90 / 40-75 reflects the wide heads-up defence and button raising. Aggression is a percentage of postflop actions, 50-66 (heads-up 50-70). WTSD is 40-55 heads-up and 30-42 / 28-40 at bigger tables. W$SD is about 46-57. The justifications are plain, original single sentences and agree with their numbers ('one hand in four' about 25%, 'one in six' about 17%). The TAG harness numbers sit inside the VPIP/PFR/Aggression/W$SD ranges at all three sizes. WTSD of about 94% is outside on purpose: qa.md Q-2 / D-2 moves that check to TASK-7.32, and the docs say so. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings: one MINOR (the slow test uses Math.round, not statTenths, and has a console.log) and two NITs.
